statements.title: About this report
statements.text: ClearFEA is a general-purpose finite element analysis tool. This report gives the numbers it computed for the model, materials, loads and supports set up by the report's author. It does not compare them with any design code, standard or acceptance criterion, and it states no judgement on the part. Whether the model represents the real part and its use, and what the results mean for it, is for the engineer responsible for the work to decide.
statements.source: DECISIONS.md Positioning (a general-purpose analysis tool; never a pass/fail or code-compliance verdict); CLAUDE.md hard rules

statements.title: Software versions
statements.text: This run was prepared with ClearFEA {clearfea}. The mesh was made by Gmsh {gmsh} with OpenCASCADE {occt}. The solver input (deck format {deckFormat}) was written by ClearFEA from the setup shown in this report and solved by CalculiX {calculix} with the {solver} equation solver.
statements.source: DECISIONS.md Positioning (reports carry software and solver versions); the run's recorded versions (ADR-032) and frozen solver (ADR-063 item 2)

statements.title: Verification
statements.text: ClearFEA is checked against verification cases with analytical or published reference values, each with a stated tolerance; the cases, their references, tolerances and the values ClearFEA computed are listed at {verificationUrl}. Those cases are simplified models: they show how closely the software reproduces known answers, not how closely this model represents its part.
statements.source: DECISIONS.md Positioning (reports carry a link to verification results); docs/VERIFICATION_RESULTS.md, the published results page (M9.7)

notes.title: Stresses near bonded faces
notes.text: The bodies of this model are meshed separately and joined at their bonded faces by tie constraints: each node of one face follows the other face, whose mesh does not match it. Displacements and forces, and in a thermal analysis temperatures and heat, are carried across each bond, but stresses within one or two elements of a bonded face are less accurate than elsewhere in the model. In a test of a bar in uniform tension made of two blocks bonded end to end, with 5 mm elements on one side and 3 mm on the other, the stress at the bonded nodes was 13% below to 12% above the exact value with 10-node elements, and 7% below to 4.5% above with 4-node elements; from 8 mm away it was within 0.1% and 0.6%. Read stresses at a bonded face with this in mind. Away from the bonds, the verification cases with bonded bodies (V-11, V-12, and V-27 for heat) match their references within the same tolerances as single-body cases.
notes.source: DECISIONS.md ADR-060 item 9 (two-block bar, nu = 0.3, 5 mm against 3 mm elements); docs/VERIFICATION.md V-11, V-12
